chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'But if you are in danger, then (perform your prayer) on foot or on horseback' [2:239], 'How should he pray?' and 'What should he say when he fears from a predatory beast or a thief, how should he pray?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should say Takbir and indicate with a gesture of his head.'

key_terms.يُكَبِّرُ: He says Takbir (exclaims Allah is Great)

ai.seo_question: How should one perform prayer when fearing danger from animals or thieves?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the practical application of Salat al-Khasf by specifying that when facing imminent danger from beasts or thieves, the prayer is performed primarily through verbal Takbir and head gestures (i'ma') rather than full physical bowing and prostration. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on flexibility and ease (rukhas) in worship, prioritizing the preservation of life and alertness to danger while maintaining the essential structure of the prayer.
